title: AI News Radar
description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs.

items.title: The Trump administration's proposal to curb China's remote access to AI chips rattles Southeast Asia, threatening a data center boom fueled by Chinese companies (New York Times)
items.content_text: The U.S. Commerce Department released a 132-page policy requiring overseas data center operators to obtain U.S. licenses before providing significant computing power to Chinese entities, effective in 90 days. This move aims to close loopholes allowing Chinese firms to bypass semiconductor export restrictions by leasing capacity in Southeast Asia, while Nvidia has established a specialized committee to oversee national security and export compliance.

items.title: Google signs a $500M+ deal to secure 50MW of geothermal power from Quaise Energy in Oregon, starting as early as 2030, to support its data centers in the state (Benoît Morenne/Wall Street Journal)
items.content_text: Google signed a power purchase agreement with Quaise Energy for 50MW of superhot geothermal power from the Project Obsidian site in Oregon. The initiative utilizes millimeter-wave drilling technology to access deep-crust thermal energy, targeting a 2030 commercial grid connection to provide resilient, carbon-free energy for data centers.

items.title: Sources: the Trump administration is moving forward with an FCC proposal to ban US imports of new Chinese optical transceiver models, despite Big Tech pushback (Reuters)
items.content_text: The Trump administration is advancing an FCC proposal to prohibit imports of new Chinese optical transceivers. This regulatory move seeks to isolate critical telecommunications infrastructure from Chinese hardware supply chains, persisting despite significant lobbying pushback from Big Tech regarding procurement costs and operational impacts.

items.title: Sequoia, Greenoaks Lead Isomorphic Lab’s $5 Billion Funding Round
items.content_text: Isomorphic Labs announced a $5 billion Series C financing round, co-led by Sequoia Capital and Greenoaks, with participation from Alphabet and Andreessen Horowitz. The capital will scale its proprietary drug design engine, IsoDDE, and advance its AI-generated therapeutic pipeline for oncology and immunology into clinical trials.

items.title: Hollywood VFX artists and studios are adopting AI and ML tools to streamline rotoscoping, a tedious process that can cost up to $75K for a one-minute scene (Matt Stevens/New York Times)
items.content_text: Tedious. Mind-numbing. Soul-destroying. Ask visual-effects artists in Hollywood and most will agree: The task known as rotoscoping, while essential, is no fun. Perhaps that is why an industry that has at times had its pitchforks out for everything artificial intelligence seems open to the idea that the technology can alleviate this particular burden. items.title: Hollywood VFX artists and studios are adopting AI and ML tools to streamline rotoscoping, a tedious process that can cost up to $75K for a one-minute scene (Matt Stevens/New York Times)
items.content_text: Hollywood visual effects studios are increasingly adopting AI and ML tools to automate rotoscoping, a labor-intensive process that can cost $75,000 per minute of footage. By leveraging algorithms for object isolation and tracking, studios are drastically reducing production timelines and human-intensive workloads in post-production.

items.title: OpenAI partners with NATO's NCIA to detect bugs, probe suspicious activity, and deploy fixes under its Daybreak program; NATO uses up to 300B tokens per month (Mauro Orru/Wall Street Journal)
items.content_text: Under the company's Daybreak program government agencies and enterprise customers can access advanced models for cybersecurity work

items.title: AI Startup for Bankers Raises Funds at $1.5 Billion Value
items.content_text: Model ML has raised fresh capital, reaching a valuation of $1.5 billion. The company develops AI agents specialized in automating repetitive backend tasks for investment banks, consulting firms, and private equity investors.

items.title: An analysis of 350+ Amazon holiday deals: 29.1% were priced the same or higher than in the prior 30 days, and ~60% had no savings compared to the prior 90 days (Groundwork Collaborative)
items.content_text: Groundwork Collaborative analyzed over 350 Amazon holiday deals, finding that 29.1% of items were priced the same or higher than in the prior 30 days, and approximately 60% offered no savings compared to the 90-day average.

items.title: Technology
items.content_text: President Xi Jinping and Prime Minister Mark Carney (Canadian PM) met in Shenzhen to expand tariff relief on agriculture and steel exports. This pact aims to reduce Canada's economic over-reliance on the U.S. and secure a more resilient cross-border supply chain.

items.title: Chinese records: Alice Huang's husband Kang Wei built a state-backed data center network in China, with proposed investment exceeding $9B between 2021 and 2024 (Lingling Wei/Wall Street Journal)
items.content_text: Kang Wei has built a data center network centered on Century Longteng, with proposed investments exceeding $9 billion in China between 2021 and 2024. The project, backed by state-linked entities and featuring a strategic partnership with Huawei, underscores China's strategic shift toward building an autonomous computing infrastructure amidst U.S. export controls.

items.title: Rogue Agents Hacked His Company. Why Is Clément Delangue So Optimistic About AI?
items.content_text: Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue warns that the concentration of compute and talent is entrenching closed-source AI dominance. He revealed that Hugging Face successfully diagnosed a cyberattack by using an open-weight Chinese model, GLM 5.2, highlighting the strategic necessity of open-source models for technical independence and security audits.

items.title: A look at Anthropic's data center network plans, dubbed Anthropic Direct, committing $900B+ through 2045; docs show it will lease 875K TPUs for $7.2B per year (Financial Times)
items.content_text: Anthropic has disclosed its 'Anthropic Direct' initiative in S-1 filings, aiming to move away from total reliance on cloud providers by leasing dedicated data centers and directly procuring AI accelerators. The company plans to commit over $900 billion through 2045, with immediate steps including leasing 875,000 TPUs at an annual cost of $7.2 billion to secure physical infrastructure control.

items.title: AI Told These Ex-Google Guys How to Build a Billion-Dollar Weapons Business
items.content_text: Tiberius Aerospace, founded by former Google and Apple executives, has secured $85 million in Series A funding. The firm utilizes AI simulations to accelerate the development of offensive weapons, specifically its 'Sceptre' long-range artillery system, aiming to align production cycles with battlefield innovation needs to break current tactical stalemates.

items.title: Sources: Nvidia Developer Tech Director Nader Khalil wrote to board arguing that failing to reinstate Jensen Huang could cost Nvidia "irreplaceable talent" (Wall Street Journal)
items.content_text: Nader Khalil, Director of Developer Technology at Nvidia, formally addressed the company's board and approximately 60 of Jensen Huang’s direct reports, expressing grave concerns regarding the potential departure of CEO Jensen Huang. The letter contends that Huang’s exit would trigger a cascade of departures among irreplaceable technical talent, jeopardizing Nvidia’s dominance in the AI computing market.

items.title: Sources: Nvidia warns customers that the proposed Remote Access Security Act could subject chip buyers to US legal action if Chinese companies access AI chips (Kai Nicol-Schwarz/CNBC)
items.content_text: Nvidia has warned customers that the proposed Remote Access Security Act (RASA) would expand export controls to cloud-based GPU access, subjecting both providers and users to U.S. legal action for non-compliance. To mitigate regulatory risk, Nvidia has implemented a strict policy prohibiting clients from renting out more than 50% of their GPU capacity to Chinese entities.

items.title: Nvidia's board establishes a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee to oversee national security policies, export control compliance, and more (Nvidia Newsroom)
items.content_text: NVIDIA's Board of Directors has established the National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee, chaired by Suzanne Nora Johnson, with Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri as members. This committee will provide direct board-level oversight for the company's National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team to manage global trade risks.

items.title: Oakland-based Numa, which builds an AI platform to manage car dealership customer service, raised a $45M Series C, a source says at a $500M post-money valuation (Camila Grigera Naón/Fortune)
items.content_text: Oakland-based AI startup Numa raised $45 million in a Series C round led by Blue Cloud Ventures, reaching a $500 million post-money valuation. The company develops an AI operating system that integrates with dealership software to automate appointment scheduling, inventory management, and warranty paperwork to address inefficiencies in automotive retail.

items.title: Meta says it modified Instagram's recommendation systems in India to show less sexual and violent content, after New Delhi called for tighter content checks (Reuters)
items.content_text: Meta Platforms has fine-tuned Instagram's recommendation algorithms for the Indian market by deploying advanced AI models to proactively detect and restrict violent and sexually suggestive content across Reels, Explore, and Feed. This adjustment follows a regulatory advisory from the Indian Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology regarding the scrutiny of algorithmic ranking and content amplification.

items.title: China taps US AI models to train homegrown rivals as chip curbs bite
items.content_text: Chinese entities are adopting increasingly sophisticated ways to use output from leading American AI models to train domestic competitors, as Beijing seeks workarounds to tightening US curbs on advanced chips.

items.title: Nvidia unveils its Rubin HPC GPU with "more than 50,000" CUDA cores, up from 28,672 in the current Rubin GPU, for agentic workflows and scientific simulations (Jeffrey Kampman/Tom's Hardware)
items.content_text: Nvidia unveiled its Rubin HPC GPU designed for scientific simulation and agentic workflows, featuring over 50,000 CUDA cores and NVLink 7 interconnect technology. The architecture utilizes a multi-die configuration to scale compute density and minimize idle resources, with a market release scheduled for 2028.

items.title: US releases details of Megaspeed probe, says investigation began in 2024
items.content_text: WASHINGTON, Nov 16 (Reuters) - The US Commerce Department and Justice Department released information on Sunday about an investigation into Singapore-based company Megaspeed, saying the probe began in 2024.

items.title: Analysis: Amazon's $17B+ planned investment in Ohio data centers is at risk after midterm voters passed restriction measures affecting three proposed projects (Rafe Rosner-Uddin/Financial Times)
items.content_text: Amazon's plan to deploy 1.8 gigawatts of data center capacity in Ohio faces administrative stagnation after voters approved 21 restrictive measures in recent midterm elections, threatening $17 billion in infrastructure investments. This grassroots 'NIMBY' backlash signifies a shift from isolated incidents to systemic regulatory friction, forcing hyperscalers to confront escalating community opposition and compliance costs in energy-intensive infrastructure expansion.

items.title: Meta is testing Direct, a standalone messaging app for Instagram that doesn't require an existing Instagram account to use, in Thailand and Turkey (Karissa Bell/Engadget)
items.content_text: Meta is testing a standalone messaging app named Direct in Thailand and Turkey, which decouples Instagram’s inbox and allows users to register without an existing Instagram account. The move seeks to capture users outside the current ecosystem while integrating parental controls and safety monitoring features.

items.title: Anthropic tells investors Claude Mythos Preview got its AI running on AMD GPUs in ~3 days with "basically no human intervention", vs. the usual 6-12 months (Shane Downing/Tom's Hardware)
items.content_text: Anthropic Chief Compute Officer Tom Brown announced that using Claude Mythos Preview, the company reduced the time required to port models to AMD GPUs from 6-12 months to roughly 3 days with minimal human intervention. This strategy aims to bypass the CUDA-centric lock-in and operationalize a heterogeneous compute pool comprising Nvidia GPUs, AMD hardware, Google TPUs, and AWS Trainium.

items.title: Filing: Leopold Aschenbrenner's hedge fund Situational Awareness, after nearly blowing up, loaded back up on AI stocks at the end of Q3; all have since plunged (Sean Conlon/CNBC)
items.content_text: Leopold Aschenbrenner, founder of Situational Awareness, re-entered the market at the end of Q3 following a summer liquidation, aggressively acquiring AI-focused assets. Regulatory filings reveal a $440 million stake in SharonAI alongside equity in Cleanspark, IREN, Bitdeer, and Fermi, plus call options in memory chip and data center energy plays, all of which have faced significant market sell-offs since October.

items.title: Sources: Jensen Huang's daughter remains in a senior Nvidia role; before Jensen Huang resigned, she was his de facto chief of staff with considerable authority (New York Times)
items.content_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned following revelations of inappropriate relationships involving a client linked to Chinese intelligence and an internal executive. Colette Kress has assumed the role of interim CEO while the company faces a management crisis regarding the unchecked authority of Huang's daughter, Madison Huang, who acted as a de facto chief of staff and exerted disproportionate influence over senior executives.

items.title: macOS 27.3 beta warns if an app would get full device control, nudging users to "Choose Apps" for the app to control instead, brought on by AI apps' popularity (Juli Clover/MacRumors)
items.content_text: Apple introduced stricter compliance requirements for Full Disk Access and Device Control APIs in the macOS 15.3 beta. Developers must refine onboarding processes to handle granular access permissions, specifically targeting AI agents to mitigate risks of unauthorized data exposure in emails, messages, and browsing history.

items.title: Exclusive-DOJ to review DoorDash-Instacart merger, sources say
items.content_text: Nov 16 (Reuters) - The US Department of Justice will review DoorDash's proposed acquisition of Instacart, according to two people familiar with the matter, bringing antitrust scrutiny to the multibillion-dollar grocery delivery tie-up.
